source.title: Function space analysis of deep learning representation layers

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Measures how a smoothness statistic changes when training labels are randomly corrupted, bearing on V4 using Besov smoothness rather than test error or training error as the outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper reports changes in training-set Besov smoothness and wavelet approximation sparsity under label corruption. It does not report training error, test error, fitting of random labels, training time, unstructured inputs, regularization comparisons, or learning order.
record.test_reason: The paper uses the original random-label finding to motivate a corruption diagnostic. Its own corruption experiments measure representation smoothness and wavelet sparsity, not training fit, test error, optimization time or learning order. These measures do not test V4 or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report decreasing smoothness with increasing label randomization and propose smoothness analysis as a corruption diagnostic. Their statement that convergence does not establish generalization or reveal corruption relies on the cited original study, rather than convergence measurements reported here.
record.recipe_differences: Computes wavelet approximation error and Besov smoothness of training-set representations, rather than measuring training/test error after fitting random labels as in the original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: Last-inner-layer Besov smoothness decreases across nominal label-randomization levels of 0–40%: 0.28 to 0.03 for MNIST and 0.204 to 0.003 for CIFAR10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label randomization reduces the measured Besov smoothness of training-set representations in these networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 and Figure 6 report that less-corrupted MNIST representations require fewer wavelet terms for comparable approximation precision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label randomization reduces wavelet approximation sparsity in the measured representations.

record.problems: The corruption experiment reports smoothness and sparsity, not training or test error. Corruption levels stop at 40%; no results for 100% random labeling. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Figure 6's precision-error curves are not numerically available in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance and unchanged training settings.
Training-time ratios and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across corruption levels through complete random labeling.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of shared-pattern learning and noise memorization.

record.verdict_notes: The stated corruption percentages are fractions selected for random relabeling; a randomly drawn label can equal the original label. Figure 6 measures wavelet approximation error, not neural-network classification error.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or training/test error results.
No training-time comparison or convergence slowdown results.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Reports smoothness and sparsity for corruption levels through 40%, not training-set fit or test error, and not corruption through all labels.
No weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation comparison.
No analysis of learning order or comparison of learned real-label patterns with noise memorization.
